title: The 25 Best Right Backs in World Soccer—Ranked
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By SI FC StaffJun 30, 2025Reece James is one of the leading right backs across world soccer. / Rob Newell/CameraSport/Getty ImagesLegendary Italian striker Gianluca Vialli once theorized that the right back was the worst player on any team. If they had more defensive nous they would be moved infield while a superior attacking outlet would line up as a winger. Even a left back has the added whiff of mystique by being left footed.

But as modern day soccer has evolved since Vialli’s retirement, incorporating flexible formations that change whether or not your team is in possession, it’s become increasingly important for fullbacks to be able to not only charge up and down the flank, but also tuck inside as an extra ball-playing midfielder.
Luckily, we’re blessed with an era of players who have taken that challenge in their stride, transforming the position into one of the most unique and important roles going.
It makes nailing down the top 25 right backs in the business all the more difficult, yet Sports Illustrated are here to do exactly that.

Jeremie Frimpong’s stock has fallen since joining the Reds. / Bill Barrett/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesJeremie Frimpong rose to prominence under the tutelage of Xabi Alonso at Bayer Leverkusen, where the speedy Dutch international was deployed as an all-action right wing back. It’s a role in which he thrived. Frimpong delivered 59 goal involvements in 131 appearances for the Spaniard and was rewarded with a move to Liverpool ahead of the 2025–26 season, where he was tasked with replacing the creativity of Trent Alexander-Arnold. Unfortunately, an injury-riddled debut campaign limited his involvement and impact, and Frimpong has been fighting an uphill battle since. He’s still yet to rediscover his mojo at Anfield and has struggled in a flat back four.

Michael Kayode continues to blossom in west London. / Mike Egerton/PA Images/Getty ImagesMichael Kayode’s ascent has been rapid, but hardly unexpected. Ever since achieving regular first-team soccer aged 16 at fourth division Italian side Gozzano, the right back has been tipped for the very top. Fiorentina couldn’t believe their luck as they poached him from the Serie D outfit in 2023. Just two years later, the Viola had sold him to Brentford for $20 million, and that’s where Kayode has been blossoming ever since. An athletic frame, powerful stride and handy long throw have proven instrumental to Brentford’s continued overperformance, and Kayode has deservedly been recognized by the Italian national team more recently as his stock rises with each passing match.

Nordi Mukiele has proven transformative for Sunderland’s defense. / George Wood/Getty ImagesSunderland’s stunning 2025–26 season—from relegation favorites to European qualifiers—was built on some shrewd summer recruitment, and Nordi Mukiele was one of the smartest additions.Signed from Bayer Leverkusen for a bargain $12.8 million, the former Paris Saint-Germain fullback quickly settled in on Wearside, bringing defensive solidity, attacking intent and a seriously dangerous long throw.And the best part? He’s still only in his twenties.

Nahuel Molina is often superior for his country.  / Marco Canoniero/LightRocket/Getty ImagesYou don’t become an Argentina regular without being a pretty decent player. Nahuel Molina may not be the most high-profile right back in the business, but he’s an incredibly steady option for his country and now Roma. Molina has won the World Cup and two Copa América titles with Argentina, consistently impressing with his attacking contributions. Silverware has been less forthcoming at club level, but he still proved a valuable asset for Atlético Madrid before his exit.

João Cancelo is now a permanent Barcelona player.  / DAMIR SENCAR/AFP/Getty ImagesSome of the things João Cancelo has done with the ball at his feet defy belief. It’s what makes his sharp decline so puzzling.There was and still is a rawness to Cancelo’s game that facilitates unpredictability every time he steps onto the field. The Portugal international is far from the best defensive right back in the world, but his work in possession is just obscene.Having hit lofty heights at Manchester City, a public fall-out led to loan spells at Bayern Munich and Barcelona, before he slinked away to Al Hilal in Saudi Arabia. However, he’s now returned to Catalonia permanently having impressed during a loan stint under Hansi Flick in 2025–26.

Josip Stanišić has enjoyed a trophy-laden career. / EyesWideOpen/Getty ImagesJosip Stanišic might not be the most glamorous right back in world soccer, but there’s a reason success follows him very closely. The Croatia international won three Bundesliga titles with Bayern Munich as an emerging talent, but, with his minutes limited, he was then shipped out on loan to Bayer Leverkusen for the 2023–24 campaign. Stanišić took his title-winning credentials to the BayArena and helped Leverkusen achieve their first-ever Meisterschale against the odds, before returning to Bayern and clinching two more Bundesliga crowns.

Injuries have often hampered Tino Livramento. / Stu Forster/Getty Images.Tino Livramento’s development was threatened by a devastating knee injury at a crucial stage of his Southampton career.Despite the setback, Newcastle United remained convinced of his potential, paying a hefty fee to sign him in the summer of 2023.They were proven right. Livramento has retained his explosive burst and continues to develop into a versatile, increasingly polished defender capable of operating on either side of the back line—even if injury issues continue to hamper his progress from time to time.

Celik joined Juventus in 2026. / Marco Canoniero/LightRocket/Getty ImagesZeki Çelik arrived at Roma as a Ligue 1 champion with Lille, but struggled to establish himself as a regular. José Mourinho often deployed him at center back, seemingly muting the attacking instincts that had made him such an effective fullback.That changed under Gian Piero Gasperini, who used Çelik as a wingback in his 3-5-2. The Türkiye international flourished in the role, impressing enough to earn a 2026 summer move to Juventus.He may not produce eye-catching numbers, but Çelik offers something just as valuable: reliability, versatility and an almost allergic reaction to mistakes—qualities Juventus will gladly welcome after a difficult period.

Djed Spence is an explosive presence.  / Mattia Pistoia/Inter/Getty ImagesThe 2026 World Cup was where Djed Spence finally showed the world what he’s all about.After initially being publicly berated by England manager Thomas Tuchel on the sidelines, Spence responded in spectacular fashion, emerging as one of England’s standout players—perhaps even their star of the tournament. Relentless in the press, powerful carrying the ball and devastating in the tackle, he also showcased the versatility that has defined his career.Spence has spent much of his career proving people wrong, from mixed loan spells in France and Italy to an inconsistent stint at Tottenham Hotspur. Now at Inter Milan—a club with a proud tradition of developing attacking fullbacks—he may finally have the platform to earn the recognition he deserves.

Julian Ryerson is an excellent creator. / STEFAN KOOPS/EYE4IMAGES/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesBorussia Dortmund’s set-piece specialist is not a character that can easily get carried away. “It’s not all that difficult,” the Norway international said of setting up his teammates. “I just have to place the ball in the right spot. The others finish it off.”Dortmund’s forward line gobbled up a glut of Ryerson’s nonchalant chance creation during the most creatively prolific campaign of his entire career—by quite some distance. The defender managed 18 assists during the 2025–26 term, which was 11 more than he conjured during his previous 10 seasons combined.

Daniel Muñoz has been excellent in England. / Joe Prior/Visionhaus/Getty ImagesDaniel Muñoz is one of world soccer’s most underrated talents. A late bloomer who spent much of his career in Colombia before moving to Genk in 2020, the speedy right back then became a star at Crystal Palace.Thriving as a wingback, Muñoz is a menace going forward, combining relentless overlapping runs with excellent distribution. He played a key role in Palace’s FA Cup triumph in 2024–25 and Europa Conference League win in 2025–26, quickly becoming a fan favorite at Selhurst Park.That was until he joined Nottingham Forest ...

Malo Gusto is a major attacking threat. / Adam Davy/PA Images/Getty ImagesChelsea are absolutely blessed at right back, with Malo Gusto the first of three stars from the position on this list.Technically, there’s an argument that he’s the most gifted of the trio. A sublime first touch, silky skills, excellent crossing and the intelligence to invert into midfield, Gusto has all the tools of a modern elite fullback.The problem? Consistency—particularly in the final third. One minute he’s putting the ball on a striker’s plate; the next, he’s sending it into Row Z.When he’s on it, though, Gusto is genuinely world-class.

Palestra is already impressing in Chelsea blue. / Ryan Pierse/Getty ImagesHeading into the 2025–26 season, Marco Palestra was a baby-faced 20-year-old who couldn’t even crack Italy’s under-21 squad, let alone Atalanta’s senior team. By season’s end, he was a full-fledged international and had earned himself a big-money move to Chelsea.“It has been a wonderful year that changed my life,” he succinctly summed up.The tireless fullback-turned-wingback is a human pendulum, constantly shuttling up and down the right flank with seemingly endless energy.

Ben White is a steady presence. / Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesEyebrows were raised when Arsenal forked out around $69 million for the services of Ben White in 2021, but the defender has more than repaid that fee through his performances at the Emirates Stadium.Be it as a right back or center back, White has always been solid, but his ability to learn and add new facets to his game make the former Brighton & Hove Albion star one of the most flexible right backs around.The England international also makes those around him better, with Bukayo Saka and Martin Ødegaard much improved when their flexible triangle on the right-hand side is completed by White.
